approach: Use runtime phases: identify stove table 1 and its control; establish OFF/ON evidence; measure local control geometry; approach; actuate incrementally; withdraw; verify. The pictured rear lever is a candidate, not a stored observation or assumed joint. Helpers: observe(predicate), fit_local, make_candidates, move_lease, check_effect, and commit. Prefer a closed-finger tangential push on a confirmed rotary lever, avoiding unnecessary grasping. Close jaws away from contact and acknowledge delivery. Use measured straight-line pressing only if runtime evidence instead identifies a push control. An already-ON observation bypasses actuation but not final verification. Persist phase intent, measurements and acknowledged physical state, not a stored trajectory.
observations: Every api.review supplies fields, explicit subject descriptions, finite enums including unknown, and named points/regions within its capacity. Request only needed evidence: stove identity, control type, base/pivot, lever tip and side patches, nearby support/obstacles, and burner/indicator baseline. Separate same-body identity, landmark correspondence, visible obstruction, and incomplete visibility. Validate points membership and measurement_errors before fitting; use api.point/cloud and camera calibration as needed. Observe returns valid, contradicted, or unknown at every call site; malformed programming inputs are not sensor uncertainty. Save camera, frame_id, physical landmark definitions and componentwise uncertainty. Control motion invalidates lever geometry, not automatically the stationary stove base; contact can invalidate base stationarity too. A newly identified lever patch may anchor a prospective differential test without recovering old vertex indices, but cannot establish past motion.
geometry: Use geo.plane coefficients for visible support/control planes, geo.circle_xy only for adequately sampled horizontal circular bases, and geo.rotation/pad_position with fresh own_geometry for the finger envelope. Infer a pivot only from supported geometry; retain ambiguous pivot/direction hypotheses. Boundary depth must agree with interior surfaces; api.plane_point is allowed only for visibly identified planar landmarks. Search up to six configurations: two accessible sides and three heights derived from measured contact and support intervals. For translated contact band [a+t,b+t], side [c,d], overlap m requires c+m-b <= t <= d-m-a, with 0<m<=min(b-a,d-c). Intersect this with finger/support constraints. Propagate shared pivot, depth, orientation and controller uncertainties without duplicate penalties. Distinguish nominal slack, conservative slack and observed response. Derive tangential stroke lengths and stopping tolerances from remaining overlap and curvature; a failed conservative bound triggers informative sensing or a justified bounded probe, not an impossibility claim.
gate_dependencies: Identification needs current target/control evidence, not all scene geometry. A noncontact approach needs a locally justified finger envelope and absence of observed obstruction; missing visibility is not certified clearance. Contact requires supported control geometry, reachable overlap and a locally admissible stroke, not proof the switch will move. The first short push produces the differential witness: independently measured lever displacement relative to its base versus measured hand displacement. A positive response supports subsequent locally remeasured strokes; no response is an observed failed trial, while hidden features are unknown. Withdrawal needs the current contact configuration and an unobstructed local escape direction. Completion requires post-withdrawal selector relation and an unambiguous visible ON effect, such as burner/indicator activation relative to baseline, after acknowledged settling steps; TCP arrival alone never suffices.
bounded_recovery: At every unknown observation, allow at most two alternatives: different visible points/view, then a bounded observation-producing move justified locally. Do not repeat unchanged occlusion; preserve valid partial evidence. Rejected configurations advance through the finite candidate set, with at most four physical trials and three short, remeasured stroke leases per trial. Reverse tangential direction only after stopping and withdrawing from a contradicted contact; never push through an observed obstruction or stall. Cap reviews at 20, control updates at 180 and branch choices at four, further limited by live budgets; reserve four reviews and 30 updates for withdrawal/verification. Check route length against selected increments and lease capacity, revising remaining route bounds if increments shrink. Commit jaw transitions and possible-contact state before fallible observations. Repairs resume that state without reset. Use at most eight checkpoints under 8 KB each and a 12-entry diagnostic window. Exhaustion, unsupported geometry, observed failure and unresolved effect receive distinct incomplete evidence.
jev_contract: Program features contain phase, selected configuration, measured local geometry, uncertainty/slack values, provenance, permitted motion and expected observation. api.choose may select candidate_a, candidate_b, observe or stop from explicitly described, currently admissible alternatives; it supplies no images, measurements or Python evaluation. Every physical update uses api.control, or api.drive for fixed-feature noncontact leases with max_calls<=40. Contact strokes use individual control updates. Supply exactly x,y,z,rx,ry,rz,gripper questions: explicit axis instructions map increase/decrease/within_tolerance to positive/negative/hold; gripper uses open/close/keep. Dispatch Jev answers unchanged. Choose legal controller limits and tolerances from geometry; do not repeat corrections suppressed by deadband. Save full api.state before leases; receipt before/after are TCP lists, not states. Record acknowledged_steps, choices and residuals, then independently remeasure control motion and final effects. Return completion_proposed and JSON-compatible evidence; model interpretation is not native task evaluation.
